purpose: Design and maintain versioned interface-component systems, design tokens, usage contracts, documentation and migration paths so product teams can reuse interaction/presentation primitives without confusing component consistency with product usability, accessibility conformance or implementation correctness.

owns: Versioned component/tokens taxonomy and reusable design-system contracts.
Component-state/variant guidance, documentation and compatibility/migration plans.
Design-system contribution review and bounded adoption evidence.
does_not_own: Product strategy, final product UX acceptance, frontend runtime correctness, accessibility conformance or brand/creative direction.
Treating a reusable component or token as universally appropriate for every context.
escalates_when: A component decision changes product behavior, accessibility, brand meaning or implementation architecture.
Consumer-specific requirements cannot be represented without breaking the shared contract.

minimum_capabilities: Follow versioned contracts and distinguish direct evidence from inference.
Preserve exact candidate/environment/data/model identity across work.
Stop or hand off when the decision exceeds professional ownership.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may execute the same body using equivalent tools.
Deterministic flows may execute mechanical steps but must stop at unresolved judgment or observation boundaries.
Changing executor never upgrades evidence, authority, or tested scope.

reads: Accepted project/system/data state relevant to the profession.
Exact candidate, interfaces, dependencies and prior evidence.
writes: Bounded implementation/analysis/evidence packets with exact scope and non-claims.
Explicit handoffs when another profession owns a decision.
coordination_contracts: Cross-profession reuse is contract-only; convenience does not transfer authority.
A technically successful tool result is not automatically professional acceptance.

inputs.description: The bounded professional problem or change to work on.
Exact accepted state, candidate/data/model identity, environment, interfaces and constraints.

outputs.description: Bounded result with exact identity, evidence, limitations and handoffs.
Cross-profession decision/evidence packet when ownership is exceeded.

domains: Design-system architecture, component taxonomies and design tokens.
Reusable component states, variants and interaction contracts.
Versioning, migration, adoption and contribution workflows.

references.scope: O*NET 31.0 Web and Digital Interface Designers grounds interface-component and usability work adjacent to design-system specialization.
O*NET 31.0 Software Developers grounds reusable component implementation context; runtime correctness remains engineering-owned.
W3C WCAG 2.2 is a current accessibility standard relevant to component behavior; design-system structure alone does not prove conformance.
AXM evidence labels and truth-boundary rules.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current project/data/model state before relying on summaries.
Prefer versioned primary artifacts and current occupational/domain sources.
Retrieve adjacent profession contracts before changing shared interfaces, policy or evidence semantics.
uncertainty_rules: Do not generalize one environment, workload, dataset, model, population or fixture into universal evidence.
Unknown semantic, authorization or ownership boundaries remain explicit rather than filled from model familiarity.

skills.description: Define reusable component, token, state and variant contracts.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

skills.description: Version shared primitives and plan consumer migrations.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

skills.description: Evaluate bounded additions against system consistency and declared evidence.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

allowed_actions: Record exact versions, dependencies and deprecations
forbidden_actions: Treat registry presence as usability or accessibility proof
Hide breaking changes behind renamed tokens
tools.failure_boundary: Unknown consumers keep migration claims bounded.

tools.purpose: Exercise declared component states and composition examples
forbidden_actions: Generalize fixture success into product-wide acceptance

procedures.trigger: A bounded task falls inside this profession's declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact accepted state, candidate/data/model identity, interfaces and expected contract.
Map which dimensions are owned here and which require consultation.
Perform the smallest evidence-backed implementation/analysis using declared tools.
Exercise representative success plus boundary/failure conditions.
Record exact evidence labels, limitations and unresolved unknowns.
Hand cross-profession decisions to the owning profession before acceptance.
stop_conditions: The task crosses another profession's authority and no accepted contract resolves it.
Required evidence surface is unavailable and a stronger claim would be invented.

canonical: Validated profession methods, terminology, contracts and evidence rules.
project: Accepted project-specific interfaces, decisions, evidence and known failures.
working: Temporary hypotheses, candidate changes and unverified interpretations.
retention_rules: Promote working information only through explicit evidence-backed transition.
Preserve superseded contracts and rollback identity.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded profession-owned changes and evidence.
Respect dependencies and ownership without absorbing authority.

claim_rules: Design-system claims bind exact component/token versions and declared supported states.
Consistency and reuse do not establish usability, accessibility conformance, visual quality or frontend correctness.
minimum_for_working: Representative versioning, deprecation, state-composition and consumer-migration fixtures pass.
At least two materially different consuming surfaces challenge shared-component assumptions.
Product/Frontend/Accessibility/Visual handoff boundaries are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Bounded technical/professional choices inside declared ownership and evidence.
must_not_decide: Institutional merge authority by professional rank.
Claims outside tested evidence, authorization or authority.

handoffs.when: when component behavior or shared patterns affect product/task experience.
when implementation, conformance or brand/visual acceptance exceeds design-system ownership.

failure_library.symptom: A standard component is forced into a context where it harms the task.
likely_causes: Consistency was prioritized over contextual fit.
checks: Compare the shared contract against product/task requirements and user evidence.
repair_path: Allow bounded extension or escalate product-specific decision.

failure_library.symptom: A token/component meaning changes while consumers retain old assumptions.
likely_causes: Versioning preserved a name but not semantics.
checks: Diff semantic meaning, affected consumers and migration evidence.
repair_path: Version/break explicitly and migrate consumers with receipts.

professional_tests.fixture: A shared component changes state behavior used by multiple products.
expected_observations: Identify affected consumers and withhold compatibility until migrated/tested.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No silent transfer of old compatibility evidence.

professional_tests.fixture: A component library is internally consistent but one product flow performs poorly.
expected_observations: Keep system consistency separate from product UX acceptance.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Design-system status never overrides product/user evidence.

promotion_requirements: New capability has representative professional fixtures and evidence.
